section: Iterate — change: R1c-2 frozen names through path()
title: Every reader and writer of a moving root file resolves it through path() (R1c-2)
context: R1c-1 gave path() a new-then-old lookup, but about 60 modules still joined the project root to a file name frozen at import (NAME = _sp.rel(key); root / NAME). After R3 moves the files into .shipwright/config/ those readers would see only the root or the pointer stub.
decision: Every join of a frozen name of a moving file calls _sp.path(key, root): codemod for constants and importers, key lists, stale-cache fallbacks (legacy literal if _sp is None else path()), indirect joins, and five readers the plan review found. audit_config (D2) and dev_server (D1) move. A guard forbids frozen-name joins in every shape it sees; the security gate reads a broken layout as zero tolerance.
consequences: Unmigrated repos read and write the same files (the root config's 2 KiB stub check now also runs at existence-only sites; writers retry the Windows sharing violation). Pathspecs, path sets, regexes and messages are R1c-3; the safety window runs until R1c-3 merges; the LayoutError surface per module is an R1e precondition before the next release (BRIEF 12.12).
rationale: Routing the reads and writes first, behind one lookup, is the smallest change that makes R3 possible; the recognition sets need both-layout reasoning and are a separate risk.
rejected: Flipping rel() to the new place (BRIEF 12.1: an unmigrated repo would read as not a Shipwright project); waiting until R3 (readers must work in both layouts before the move); a lazy function per module (same effect, more surface).
